editorial.marketOverview: The latest US cash session is Friday November 20. Reuters reported Nasdaq Composite down 5.28% and SOX down approximately 11%, while AP reported the S&P 500 down 3.7%; chip underperformance remains the strongest directional signal. The market is closed Saturday, so these figures are carried-forward Friday observations, not new quotes.
editorial.whatChanged: Compared with the prior 08:49 EST snapshot, Reuters' global markets report and Barron's November 21 weekly review corroborate the already documented broad technology selloff and policy concerns. Open Watch's curated event count and update timestamp are unchanged. No newly verified catalyst or synchronized market observation warrants a material outlook change.
editorial.marketInterpretation: Semiconductor weakness relative to QQQ, poor reported breadth and elevated volatility favor downside continuation, although the magnitude of Friday's liquidation increases short-covering risk. Friday's Treasury safe-haven bid does not establish a synchronized 10Y/2Y curve. The prior indicative +29 bp is correctly scaled but stale; FedWatch, VXN and contract-matched oil remain unverified. A reported probability of a December hike is not substituted for a direct CME reading.
editorial.threeDayPath: Monday November 23 brings reopening and flash PMIs, potentially producing either a short-covering rebound or renewed selling. Tuesday November 24 consumer confidence and ADI/Dell earnings will test demand and semiconductor leadership. Wednesday November 25 PCE, GDP and the Beige Book could shift rate expectations. These are conditional catalysts, not realized price reactions. Baseline remains bearish elevated downside risk unless QQQ and SOX/SMH recover together with better breadth and lower volatility.
editorial.bullCase: A sharp Friday washout can fuel a relief rally if PMIs and earnings beat feared outcomes. Confirmation requires synchronized QQQ and SOX/SMH gains, improving advance-decline participation and falling VXN/VIX, ideally with independently verified easing rate pressure.
editorial.bearCase: Chip leadership deterioration, weak breadth and volatility expansion could make relief rallies fragile. Disappointing PMI, hardware guidance or inflation outcomes could extend downside, but no outcome or market reaction should be assumed before release.
editorial.watchNext: At Monday's reopening collect synchronized QQQ, Nasdaq, SOX/SMH, breadth and VXN/VIX; primary-source 10Y and 2Y with percent-to-basis-point conversion; CME policy probabilities and matched Brent/WTI contracts.
